text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today as oil prices remained elevated amid Middle East tensions, though the move was modest. Over the past two weeks, the stock has climbed 6% in tandem with crude prices—U.S. oil is trading near $97 a barrel, up from around $91 two weeks ago—driven by supply disruptions. Saudi Arabia's shutdown of its East-West pipeline after drone attacks, combined with escalating regional tensions between Iran and Western powers, have kept oil prices well above $100 per barrel at times this week, supporting energy producers' margins.

The broader picture is one of volatility around geopolitical risk. While Trump has suggested oil prices will fall sharply after mid-term elections if Iran negotiations resume, those negotiations remain uncertain, and markets are pricing in continued supply tightness for now. That uncertainty—along with the gap between U.S. crude ($97) and world prices ($110)—is keeping oil elevated enough to support the sector's recent gains.
